answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable bond before it may issue claims or receive scarce resources. A grove of cedar agents sharing one operator must post a separate bond for every identity, while a trellis of reputation links lets peers slash bonds when identities coordinate fraud. The attacker therefore pays capital up front and risks losing it; creating names is cheap, but sustaining many credible identities is not. This raises the cost of Sybils without pretending to prove that bonded agents are unique humans.
